content:
With WhatsApp officially rolling out its username feature, the app now lets users save a username alongside the name and phone number when storing a contact. Here are the details.

The addition of a username field when adding new contacts is gradually being made available to some WhatsApp users

Although usernames are a staple feature on most messaging platforms, WhatsApp has only recently begun to move away from relying entirely on phone numbers to identify users.

Earlier this year, WhatsApp began rolling out a username reservation system, giving users the chance to register their preferred usernames in advance to prevent impersonation and scams once the feature went live.

A few weeks ago, WhatsApp began enabling the username feature for some iPhone users.

Now, according to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp has started supporting a username field when users add new contacts. The field appears between the first name and last name fields and the phone number field.

WABetaInfo reports:

WABetaInfo notes that the username field appears to be rolling out gradually to selected users on both the WhatsApp Beta and stable versions.

When I tested it using the latest stable version, the field was displayed, but even when the username actually exists, the system still showed a message saying "this username is not on WhatsApp".

That said, this marks WhatsApp finally catching up with its competitors and adding a feature that many considered long overdue.
